title: Science Literacy: Generative AI as Enabler of Coherence in the Teaching, Learning, and Assessment of Scientific Knowledge and Reasoning
venue: The handbook of generative AI in education: Implications for research and practice
extended_summary:
This chapter examines how generative AI could support science literacy across the K-16+ span, with a particular emphasis on K-12 science education. The central problem is the long-standing disconnect between science curriculum, instruction, and assessment, especially under contemporary standards that require students to integrate disciplinary core ideas, science and engineering practices, and crosscutting concepts. The authors argue that this challenge becomes even more important in the era of AI, because science education must now also prepare learners to understand and use AI in scientifically informed ways.

Rather than reporting a new empirical intervention study, the chapter proposes a human-in-the-loop architecture for integrating generative AI into science teaching, learning, and assessment. It discusses how AI can support teacher-facing work such as creating lesson plans, generating assessments, scoring student explanations and models, and providing formative feedback, while keeping teachers in control of pedagogical decisions. The paper distinguishes these teacher-facing uses from student-facing intelligent tutoring and open-ended learning environments that provide direct scaffolding to learners.

The discussion is grounded in K-12 science education frameworks such as the NRC Framework and NGSS, and it uses examples from recent science education AI systems, including AI-supported scoring and feedback tools and generative tools for instructional design. The authors conclude that generative AI has strong potential to improve coherence across curriculum, instruction, and assessment, but only if designed within transparent, ethical, and teacher-mediated systems that preserve human agency and align with disciplinary learning goals.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / large language model-based educational assistant used to generate instructional materials, support feedback on student work, and assist with assessment and tutoring-like scaffolding.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a human-in-the-loop generative AI approach in K-12 science education to support teachers with lesson planning, formative feedback, and assessment design; the chapter also discusses teacher-facing use for creating lesson plans and scoring/explaining short-answer assessments.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical chapter rather than an empirical evaluation, and it does not report a study design, sample, or outcomes for a specific tool. The text discusses architectures and illustrative examples instead of measured effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The chapter argues that generative AI could reduce teacher workload and support coherence across teaching, learning, and assessment, but it provides no direct outcome data or effect sizes. Impact is therefore plausible but unmeasured in this paper.
